rationale: PINS the message-tree `contains` contract at R3: a message OWNS its fields and nested messages — a TREE fact on existing grammar nodes (`message` under `message_body`, target = the nested message's own symbol). The construct is already emitted (the analyzer's message case, member `nestedType`), and 13 fixtures fire it incidentally while resolving other questions; this fixture pins THE TREE FACT ITSELF with both negative controls, which none of them does: (1) `meta.member` is pinned as `nestedType` on the nested-message rows — no other fixture pins that metadata, so a relabel of the member key or an emission that swaps it with the field member would pass every other fixture and fail here; (2) ownership is exactly one level deep: the PACKAGE owns the top-level message and the MESSAGE owns its nested one, so a contains edge from the PACKAGE to a twice-nested type, or from a nested message to a SIBLING's member, would assert a chain as an edge — the reversed direction is forbidden because containment is the owning edge, not a transitive one; (3) a field inside the nested message is owned by ITS message, not by the outer one, so the outer message claiming the leaf field is forbidden — the exact shape an analyzer that pushed body children onto the wrong owner would produce. Expectations are hand-derived from the protobuf declaration forms, not from an analyzer run.

the tree is recursive: Branch owns Leaf exactly as Root owns Branch
the field belongs to the innermost message that declares it

forbidRelationships.note: the package does NOT own the nested message — ownership is exactly one level deep, and this row is the transitive-chain impostor: an analyzer that minted a package->deeply-nested edge would be asserting the CHAIN as an EDGE.
Root does NOT own its grandchild: the tree fact is parent-to-child, never grandparent-to-grandchild.
Root does NOT own Branch's field: pushing body children onto the wrong owner is the exact defect this forbids.
the deepest impostor: package to a twice-removed field. Any of these four rows firing means the contains walk flattened the tree.
Leaf has no group, so no #property twin exists; this row forbids a fabricated disambiguated id on a plain nested-message tree.
